html:
Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan was ruler of Abu Dhabi from 1966 and the first president of the United Arab Emirates from 1971 until his death in 2004. Emiratis call him the father of the nation.

He grew up in a poor sheikhdom and governed the Al Ain oasis for twenty years, where he was known for sharing out water fairly. When oil money came, his family replaced his brother with him, and he spent freely on housing, schools, hospitals and the greening of the desert.

He led the talks that made the federation in 1971, and Abu Dhabi's wealth held it together. He gave aid widely abroad. His son Khalifa and then Mohamed bin Zayed followed him as president.
